summary: Built 1930 as an L-4 gable-roof groundhouse in the Flathead National Forest; little used until restored and restaffed from 2010.

events.note: Chuck Manning served as the lookout in the summer of 1963
The 2014 article says 2010 was the first summer staffed since 1973
Forest Service decided to begin staffing the lookout again
NHLR says just restored at registration; firelookout.com says a restoration effort began in 2010
Leif Haugen transferred to Thoma; first summer staffed since 1973

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR (2010 registration) says the lookout has just been restored; firelookout.com says a restoration effort began in 2010. Both place the work in 2010: NHLR describes the finished state at registration and firelookout.com the start.

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1930 build, L-4 design, ground kind and NHLR registration (September 28, 2010) are supported. No source read gives public access rules or climbability, so no access or visit keys are set. The 2014 article's claim that Thoma is on the National Register of Historic Places is not confirmed by any source read (only the NHLR listing is confirmed); the story attributes the claim rather than asserting it. The 2026 article's date comes from its URL and is used as the as-of date for the staffing status. The 1963 and 1973 staffing dates come from two different articles and are not reconciled further.
